title: Robust Spin-1 Haldane Topology under Itinerant Doping
abstract: We study itinerant hole doping of the spin-$1$ Haldane symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase in two $t$--$J$ chains coupled by ferromagnetic (FM) Hund exchange. Density-matrix renormalization group calculations show that string order, a finite spin gap, and the Haldane entanglement structure coexist over a broad doping range. Combined with entanglement-entropy scaling consistent with a single gapless charge mode, these results support a metallic doped Haldane SPT with a $C1S0$ low-energy description. At low doping, short-range charge correlations reduce the density of spin-$1/2$ defect rungs, whereas at larger doping their positions become nearly uncorrelated while their spins are collectively incorporated into the correlated spin sector. The doped Haldane SPT terminates in a fully spin-polarized FM phase, which forms a reentrant pocket at high doping in the global phase diagram. Dilute-limit analyses trace the two FM boundaries to spin--charge factorization at weak Hund coupling and to rung-triplet binding with reduced pair mobility at strong Hund coupling. Our results show how mobile carriers reorganize the Haldane spin structure while preserving its characteristic signatures.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates how the spin-1 Haldane topological phase persists when holes are doped into the system. Using DMRG and Bosonization, the authors map out the phase diagram, showing that the topological order remains robust while the system develops a metallic character. The study reveals complex doping-dependent physics, including the formation of a reentrant ferromagnetic phase at high doping.
main_problem: The study investigates the robustness and evolution of the spin-1 Haldane symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase when the system is subjected to itinerant hole doping.
main_result: The doped Haldane SPT remains stable over a broad doping range, characterized by a metallic low-energy description, and its phase diagram reveals a reentrant ferromagnetic pocket at high doping.
method: The research employs advanced numerical techniques, primarily Density-Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) calculations, supplemented by Bosonization analysis to characterize the electronic and spin correlations.
model_or_system: The model consists of two t-J chains coupled by a ferromagnetic (FM) Hund exchange interaction, allowing for the study of charge and spin degrees of freedom under doping ($\delta$).
key_observables: String Order Parameter (SOP), bulk spin gap ($\Delta_s$), entanglement spectrum, and various correlation functions like hole correlations ($g_{hh}(r)$) and defect-spin correlations ($G_{dd}(r)$).
important_parameters: Doping ($\delta$), Hund coupling ($J_H$), and the AFM leg exchange coupling ($J$) are the key tuning parameters defining the phase diagram.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on extrapolating finite-size DMRG results to the thermodynamic limit and uses empirical fits to map out the boundaries of the ferromagnetic phase.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the global phase diagram in the $(J_H, \delta)$ plane, showing the coexistence of the doped Haldane SPT and FM phases, alongside plots detailing the evolution of topological and correlation diagnostics across doping levels.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system's behavior by first establishing the model and key diagnostics (DMRG/Bosonization). It then maps the global phase diagram, detailing how low doping involves short-range charge correlations, while high doping shows a crossover to collective spin incorporation, culminating in the characterization of the reentrant FM boundary.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed theoretical understanding of how topological order (Haldane SPT) can survive and reorganize in the presence of mobile charge carriers, which is crucial for understanding doped quantum magnets and correlated materials.
